title: つもり & 予定 : Intention and Plans

blocks.content: Both **つもり** and **予定** express future plans, but they differ in who made the decision and how fixed it is.

left.label: つもりです
left.description: Personal intention : an internal decision already made in your own mind. Not dependent on others.
left.example_jp: 来年、日本に行くつもりです。
left.example_en: I intend to go to Japan next year.

right.label: 予定です
right.description: Scheduled plan : often external, fixed, or coordinated with others. Suits appointments and timetables.
right.example_jp: 三時に会議が始まる予定です。
right.example_en: The meeting is scheduled to start at 3.

lines: [Dictionary form] + **つもりです**      ← intend to (personal decision)
[Negative plain] + **つもりです**       ← intend not to
[Dictionary form] + **予定です**        ← scheduled to (arranged plan)
[Noun] + の + **予定です**              ← have a plan for ~

rows.japanese: もうお酒を飲まないつもりです。
rows.romaji: Mō osake wo nomanai tsumori desu.
rows.english: I intend not to drink anymore.
I have a business trip planned next month.

rows.japanese: 飛行機は六時に到着する予定です。
rows.romaji: Hikōki wa rokuji ni tōchaku suru yotei desu.
rows.english: The plane is scheduled to arrive at 6.

blocks.content: If you made a reservation or appointment, use 予定. If you have decided something for yourself regardless of others, use つもり.
